newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to defend Ukraine in crisis, Yeltsin says.
newsitem.headline: Russia to defend Ukraine in crisis, Yeltsin says.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, who arrived in Kiev on Friday to sign a pact on bilateral relations, said before leaving that Moscow would defend Ukraine "in extreme situations".

"This is in the agreement, that we will participate together to defend Ukraine if anything happens," Yeltsin said in an interview to be broadcast later on Friday on Ukrainian television Studio 1+1 and Russian public television.

Yeltsin did not specify the conditions under which Russia would come to the aid of its fellow ex-Soviet republic. In the interview, he discussed an accord between Moscow and Kiev dividing the Soviet Black Sea Fleet and allowing Russia to lease naval facilities at the Ukrainian port of Sevastopol.
"I am in favour of us jointly providing security and helping each other in extreme situations so it is obligatory to help," Yeltsin said.

Russia has mutual defence agreements with most members of the Commonwealth of Independent States but not Ukraine, Moldova and Turkmenistan. The CIS groups the former Soviet republics except for the Baltic states.

Yeltsin's statement came three days after he signed an agreement with NATO establishing a new security relationship. The Kremlin leader, who is anxious to prevent former Soviet states from joining NATO, repeated his warning that Russia would rethink relations with the Western alliance if it sought to expand into the ex-Soviet republics.
